name: The T wave
who: Human LV wall · 1.2 cm transmural strand · 1 Hz
ref: Gima & Rudy 2002; ten Tusscher et al. 2004/2006
brief: The ECG is not the voltage of any one cell. It is the electric field of a whole wall of cells, activating and recovering at slightly different times. This is a 1.2 cm strip of left-ventricular wall, stimulated on the endocardial side and recorded by an electrode 2 cm beyond the epicardium. Right now every layer is the same, so the QRS is too narrow and the T wave points the wrong way. Give the wall its real layers.
protocol: Endocardial stimulus at t = 0; single cells pre-paced at 1 Hz; pseudo-ECG scaled so the reference QRS = 1
hint0: QRS width is set by how fast the wavefront crosses the wall. The T wave is upright when the layer activated last (the epicardium) finishes repolarising first, so the epicardium needs the shortest action potential. M cells, in the midwall, have the longest.
debrief: The pseudo-ECG is φ ∝ ∫ (−∂V/∂x) · ∂(1/r)/∂x dx: only voltage gradients along the wall make a signal. During the QRS the gradient is the activation front, so its width is the transmural conduction time, set by gap-junction coupling (Cx43). During the T wave the gradient comes from cells repolarising at different times. In a uniform wall the cells that activate last also repolarise last, and the T wave is inverted, opposite to the QRS. Real hearts invert this order with a transmural gradient of K⁺ channels: dense IKs in the epicardium (0.392 nS/pF, the value used in ten Tusscher & Panfilov 2006) and sparse IKs in midwall M cells. The interval from T peak to T end reflects transmural dispersion of repolarisation, which is a clinical marker of arrhythmia risk. This 1D strand explains the T wave. The real QRS also depends on the 3D activation sequence laid down by the Purkinje network, on the heart's geometry and on the torso, which needs whole-heart models.

lens.note: This is one epicardial cell with your wall's channel densities, uncoupled from its neighbours, so you can watch the K⁺ currents that end its action potential early. In the wall, coupling to the longer-lasting midwall cells pulls its repolarisation a little later. {@note}
